a:r.a:t: Crosstalk Between a Tyrosine Kinase Receptor and a GPCR Is an Example of Integration of Signals

p:cNvPr.descr: Diagram of the cross talk between the insulin receptor and the beta2-adrenergic receptor (or other GPCR). Diagram of the cross talk between the insulin receptor and the beta2-adrenergic receptor (or other GPCR). The reaction occurs in the cytosol, represented by a yellowish area that is bordered by the plasma membrane. The first structure, from left to right, is a brownish receptor labeled GPCR. On the left of this structure, a red line points outward. The line has an indentation in it, marked with a Y, and bonded to a red circle with a P in it. Below this is a series of molecules, labeled SHC (TAN), Grb2 (gray), Sos (gray), Ras (green), and Raf-1 (blue). From this, an arrow points downward to a blue structure labeled MEK, and another arrow points downward to a blue oval structure, labeled ERK. Another arrow points downward into the blue nucleus of the cell – this points to “altered gene expression.” Next to the GPCR receptor is the pinkish folded insulin receptor, labeled alpha and beta at the top, and with the two rounded projections extended into the cytosol. The rounded projections are bonded to 6 green Ps. The third P from the right has an arrow pointing downward to IRS-1, which has two curved arrows pointing upward to PKB. The fourth P is connected to 4 red Ps, which are connected to the two Y and two S tails on a beta-Adrenergic receptor. The PKB is also connected to the 4 red Ps via two arrows. A dashed arrow points to a fourth receptor that is similar to the beta-adrenergic receptor, except this structure is not connected to PKB or IRS-1. The text on the bottom reads, “GPCR internalization, reduced GPCR responsiveness.”

p:cNvPr.descr: Diagram E. This diagram has two side-by-side illustrations, one representing Signal 1, which has an arrow pointing down to a green triangle that sits atop a pink box representing Receptor 1, and the second representing Signal 2, which has an arrow pointing down to a green triangle ithat sits atop a pink oval representing Receptor 2. Under the illustration of Signal-Receptor 1 is the text, "[up arrow] [X] or [up-arrow] V-sub-m. Under the illustration of Signal-Receptor 2 is the text, "[down arrow] [X] or [down arrow] V-sub-m." A horizontal bracket points below to the text, "Net [delta]-[X] or [delta] V-sub-m," which is connected to a down arrow pointing to the text Response. The text accompanying the diagram reads, "Integration. When two signals have opposite effects on a metabolic characteristic such as the concentration of a second messenger X, or the membrane potential V-sub-m the regulatory outcome results from the integrated input from both receptors."
